Specific studies mentioned include the work of Elkins and Wu on angle of attack and distance-based criteria for flange climb derailment, Gilchrist and Brickle's re-examination of railway wheel-set proneness to derailment, and Sweet et al
's research on derailment mechanics and safety criteria for rail vehicle trucks
Despite these advances, further scientific research is necessary to better understand the root causes of derailments
The sources indicate that track geometry irregularities significantly impact railway vehicle safety and derailment risk
The "Track Geometry Irregularities Project Report" highlights the importance of continuous monitoring and predictive maintenance to mitigate risks and improve operational reliability

The "INVESTIGATION AND MONITORING SYSTEM FOR RAILWAY DERAILMENT" paper discusses the influence of track irregularities on the dynamic behavior of railway vehicles and the need for advanced monitoring systems

The "Running safety of a railway vehicle in the presence of random track irregularities" sources emphasize the direct relation between the power spectral density of the derailment coefficient and the lateral and angular wheelset displacements, indicating that addressing track irregularities is crucial for enhancing railway safety

The sources indicate that statistical analysis and modeling techniques have been used to develop derailment probabilities for freight trains and cars, considering factors like train length, speed, and car positioning (Anderson and Barkan, 2005)
